pairs: Oratio pauperis,
The prayer of the pauper,
cum anxius fuerit,
when he was anxious,
et in conspectu Domini effuderit precem suam.
and so he poured out his petition in the sight of the Lord.
Domine,
O Lord,
exaudi orationem meam,
hear my prayer,
et clamor meus ad te veniat.
and let my outcry reach you.
Non avertas faciem tuam a me:
Do not turn your face away from me.
in quacumque die tribulor,
In whatever day that I am in trouble,
inclina ad me aurem tuam;
incline your ear to me.
in quacumque die invocavero te,
In whatever day that I will call upon you,
velociter exaudi me.
heed me quickly.
Quia defecerunt sicut fumus dies mei,
For my days have faded away like smoke,
et ossa mea sicut cremium aruerunt.
and my bones have dried out like firewood.
Percussus sum ut fœnum,
I have been cut down like hay,
et aruit cor meum,
and my heart has withered,
quia oblitus sum comedere panem meum.
for I had forgotten to eat my bread.
A voce gemitus mei adhæsit os meum carni meæ.
Before the voice of my groaning, my bone has adhered to my flesh.
Similis factus sum pellicano solitudinis;
I have become like a pelican in solitude.
factus sum sicut nycticorax in domicilio.
I have become like a night raven in a house.
Vigilavi,
I have kept vigil,
et factus sum sicut passer solitarius in tecto.
and I have become like a solitary sparrow on a roof.
Tota die exprobrabant mihi inimici mei,
All day long my enemies reproached me,
et qui laudabant me adversum me jurabant:
and those who praised me swore oaths against me.
quia cinerem tamquam panem manducabam,
For I chewed on ashes like bread,
et potum meum cum fletu miscebam,
and I mixed weeping into my drink.
a facie iræ et indignationis tuæ:
By the face of your anger and indignation,
quia elevans allisisti me.
you lifted me up and threw me down.
Dies mei sicut umbra declinaverunt,
My days have declined like a shadow,
et ego sicut fœnum arui.
and I have dried out like hay.
Tu autem,
But you,
Domine,
O Lord,
in æternum permanes,
endure for eternity,
et memoriale tuum in generationem et generationem.
and your memorial is from generation to generation.
Tu exsurgens misereberis Sion,
You will rise up and take pity on Zion,
quia tempus miserendi ejus,
for it is time for its mercy,
quia venit tempus:
for the time has come.
quoniam placuerunt servis tuis lapides ejus,
For its stones have pleased your servants,
et terræ ejus miserebuntur.
and they will take pity on its land.
Et timebunt gentes nomen tuum,
And the Gentiles will fear your name,
Domine,
O Lord,
et omnes reges terræ gloriam tuam:
and all the kings of the earth your glory.
quia ædificavit Dominus Sion,
For the Lord has built up Zion,
et videbitur in gloria sua.
and he will be seen in his glory.
Respexit in orationem humilium
He has noticed the prayer of the humble,
et non sprevit precem eorum.
and he has not despised their petition.
Scribantur hæc in generatione altera,
Let these things be written in another generation,
et populus qui creabitur laudabit Dominum.
and the people who will be created will praise the Lord.
Quia prospexit de excelso sancto suo;
For he has gazed from his high sanctuary.
Dominus de cælo in terram aspexit:
From heaven, the Lord has beheld the earth.
ut audiret gemitus compeditorum;
So may he hear the groans of those in shackles,
ut solveret filios interemptorum:
in order that he may release the sons of the slain.
ut annuntient in Sion nomen Domini,
So may they announce the name of the Lord in Zion
et laudem ejus in Jerusalem:
and his praise in Jerusalem:
in conveniendo populos in unum,
while the people convene,
et reges,
along with kings,
ut serviant Domino.
in order that they may serve the Lord.
Respondit ei in via virtutis suæ:
He responded to him in the way of his virtue:
Paucitatem dierum meorum nuntia mihi:
Declare to me the brevity of my days.
ne revoces me in dimidio dierum meorum,
Do not call me back in the middle of my days:
in generationem et generationem anni tui.
your years are from generation to generation.
Initio tu,
In the beginning,
Domine,
O Lord,
terram fundasti,
you founded the earth.
et opera manuum tuarum sunt cæli.
And the heavens are the work of your hands.
Ipsi peribunt,
They will perish,
tu autem permanes;
but you remain.
et omnes sicut vestimentum veterascent.
And all will grow old like a garment. And,
Et sicut opertorium mutabis eos,
like a blanket, you will change them,
et mutabuntur;
and they will be changed.
tu autem idem ipse es,
Yet you are ever yourself,
et anni tui non deficient.
and your years will not decline.
Filii servorum tuorum habitabunt,
The sons of your servants will live,
et semen eorum in sæculum dirigetur.
and their offspring will be guided aright in every age.
